title: Security camera firmware contains hardcoded GitHub admin token
summary: A security camera&\#x27;s login page was found to contain a hardcoded GitHub admin token, allowing unauthorized access to the vendor&\#x27;s GitHub repository. This vulnerability highlights critical security failures in IoT devices, exposing proprietary code and potentially enabling supply chain attacks. It underscores the need for secure credential management and code review in embedded systems. The hardcoded token was embedded in the login page&\#x27;s HTML/JavaScript source, accessible to anyone viewing the page source. The token reportedly belonged to a Hanwha-branded camera, with the vendor&\#x27;s GitHub admin credentials exposed.
context: Hardcoded credentials are a known security anti-pattern where sensitive keys are embedded directly in source code. IoT devices often suffer from such vulnerabilities due to rushed development and lack of security auditing. In this case, the token not only compromizes the camera but also the vendor&\#x27;s GitHub account, risking code integrity.
discussion: Community comments express dismay at widespread insecure IoT practices, with users recommending network segmentation \(e.g., separate VLANs\) and questioning the trustworthiness of certain vendors. Some highlight similar patterns in other devices like OBD-II dongles.
